published_prior_art.cite: KleinsteuberShen2013NUJDUniqueness proves uniqueness for one fixed complete diagonal family, not overlap of separately selected honest families.
RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift gives the all-honest c=0 criterion; AkhavanEtAl2019GeometryJD gives threshold trimming without a worst-case replacement iff or causal converse.

RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift gives continuous-amplitude genericity and PerryVonKugelgenScholkopf2022SparseShift studies sparse mechanism changes, but neither gives the affine-occupancy formula under replacement.
LeNguyen2022HermitianSDC supplies a complete-family SDC test; enumerating h-subsets and unioning oracle outputs is a routine reduction.
RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1 gives the c=0 iff uniqueness condition after covariance differencing.
AndrewsCheng2013SporadicID supplies general identification-robust inference, while the stated union is a new application to the proposed compatibility map.

Afsari2008JDSensitivity is selected-model local sensitivity and AndrewsCheng2013SporadicID is general weak-identification inference; neither supplies subset-uniform rational affine-minor certificates.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition: backshift-reduction
novelty_flags.one_line: This proposition intentionally restates the c=0 BACKSHIFT identifiability theorem, so it is published-known and should remain explicitly a sanity corollary rather than be counted as novelty.

novelty_flags.label: related_work / literature_map / seed 2
novelty_flags.one_line: PerryVonKugelgenScholkopf2022SparseShift has no Theorem 4.4: its Section 4 result is Corollary 4.2 for bivariate identifiability, while multivariate graph identification is Theorem 5.3 and Corollary 5.4.

soundness_flags.label: Dcal role, thm:sharp-replacement-radius, and prose uses of “stable”
soundness_flags.one_line: The stated CP(I-D)<1 normalization is not dynamical stability: the cited BACKSHIFT paper explicitly notes that CP(B)<1 and spectral-radius stability can diverge for intersecting cycles; call it cycle-product-normalized or add the intended spectral-radius condition.

soundness_flags.label: ass:support-factorization
soundness_flags.one_line: The Perry et al. citation studies unknown subsets of changed conditional mechanisms, not a fixed binary support Z with diagonal variance factorization s_ek=Z_ek a_ek; retag this as novel and justify it, or cite a source that states this BACKSHIFT-specific condition.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3–4, equations (5)–(10) and Theorem 1, especially p. 4 equation (13)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines Dcp by unit diagonal and CP(I-D)<1 after covariance differencing, and Theorem 1 gives iff uniqueness when every pair of intervention-variance difference profiles is noncollinear.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3–5, Assumption 2.3, Corollary 4.2, Proposition 5.1, and surrounding Section 5 text
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper models each environment by an unknown subset of changed conditional mechanisms; Section 4 contains Corollary 4.2 (bivariate identifiability), whereas the multivariate MSS results begin in Section 5. It does not state Theorem 4.4 or a fixed diagonal-variance support factorization.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 4.2, equation (42), paragraphs immediately following equation (42)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article identifies outlier target matrices by a thresholded distance, updates the retained set iteratively, and expressly says it gives no convergence proof for the outlier-aware method.

source_verification_receipts.version: author preprint, arXiv:1111.7088v3; corroborates the cited IEEE TSP 2013 article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 characterizes essential uniqueness of an exact non-unitary joint diagonalizer for a fixed diagonal matrix family by profile collinearity modulus rho<1.

source_verification_receipts.version: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 43(2) (2022) journal article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article gives equivalent Hermitian SDC conditions including positive-definite feasibility of a linear Hermitian system and a numerical polynomial-time procedure for one supplied matrix family.

source_verification_receipts.version: metadata/abstract corroboration for SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 30(3) (2008); primary full text not inspected
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited article concerns sensitivity and uniqueness of nonorthogonal joint diagonalization, consistent with its limited use as a local-conditioning comparator.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 173(1) (2013) article metadata/abstract; publisher full text inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies estimators, tests, and confidence sets when parameters are unidentified on parts of the parameter space, consistent with its general identification-robust-inference role.
The paper gives generic graph-based identifiability criteria for sparse causal effects in an IV model; it is only a neighboring support-driven identification comparator.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Correct the Perry citation to Corollary 4.2 and Theorem 5.3/Corollary 5.4, then retag support factorization as a novel fixed-design restriction with a concrete experimental mechanism that makes Z prespecified and amplitudes positive.

Replace every use of “stable” for CP(I-D)<1 with “BACKSHIFT cycle-product-normalized”; if dynamical stability is substantively required, state rho(I-D)<1 separately and re-check the converse within that narrower class.

Add a genuine design result: optimize the support-incidence frontier under a stated intervention-budget constraint and prove a matching combinatorial lower bound, so the sparse-support corollary becomes an independently useful design theorem.

For the open inference programme, specify a semialgebraic input encoding and prove a terminating certificate algorithm with a complexity bound, rather than leaving the feasibility oracle as the computational interface.

recommended_next_step: Return to Stage -1 for citation/assumption and terminology repairs; retain the sharp replacement-radius theorem as the field-tier kernel and keep the c=0 reduction explicitly non-novel.
